name: Zlarong
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Zhao, Haoliang (2018) A brief introduction to Zlarong, Proc. ICSTLL-51, Kyoto Univ., 1053-1060 (not online); also Tashi Nyima & Suzuki 2019, LTBA 42(1)

new_statements.quote: For suprasegmentals, two tones high ( ˉ ) and rising ( ´ ) are distinctive, functioning as a word-tone system. Only the first two syllables of words are tone bearing units (TBU). Syllables after the third syllable of a word are atonal, which are realised as low level. An apostrophe ( ’ ) appearing between first and second syllables denotes that the second syllable is out of TBU and atonal.
new_statements.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki, Tsering Samdrup & Sonam Wangmo. 2018. Contrastive word list of three non-Tibetic languages of Chamdo: Lamo, Larong sMar, and Drag-yab sMar. Kyoto University Linguistic Research 37: 79-104. doi:10.14989/240980
new_statements.rule_in_words: Zlarong/Larong sMar is described as a word-tone language, not a stress language: a two-way (high vs rising/low) tonal contrast is carried by the first two syllables of the word, all later syllables being atonal low; some words additionally have an 'accent nucleus' after the first syllable that makes the second syllable atonal (Suzuki et al. 2024 liken this H/L + nucleus system to Kansai Japanese). Zhao 2018 (p. 1053, the language's namesake description, Renguo Twp.) instead gives a three-way word-tone system High 55 / Falling 53 / Low 31~13. No source found says anything about word stress in Zlarong itself.
new_statements.exceptions: Suzuki et al. 2022 (p. 30) and 2023 (p. 35): compounds may carry a separate tone per component morpheme; first-syllable-only tone (accent nucleus) is rare in the mTsholnga dialect. Suzuki et al. 2024 Table 3, (25)-(26): in Rongsmad the numerals 22-29 form a single TBU with the third syllable atonal, whereas in Thaya each of the two numeral morphemes keeps its own TBU; the accent nucleus is largely absent from Drag-yab sMar numerals.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word (elicited wordlist citation forms; suffixes mostly fall outside the TBU). The only explicit remark on stress in this literature is Suzuki et al. 2024 p. 79 and is phrased for the sister language Lamo, not Larong sMar: 'it has not been applied to Lamo; no linguistic realisation supports either the existence or non-existence of stress on a single syllable' — the authors present Lamo, Larong sMar and Drag-yab sMar as sharing the same suprasegmental type (two-way H/L 'just like its sister languages, Larong sMar and Drag-yab sMar', p. 67).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog zlar1234 'Zlarong' = 'Larong sMar' of Suzuki/Tashi Nyima = 'Rumei-hua' of the Changdu gazetteer; autonym m̥a55 / mə55kə55. The quoted 2018 statement describes the Phagpa dialect (Renguo Twp., Dzogang); Zhao 2018 describes the Renguo/Dongba variety; Suzuki et al. 2022/2023 describe Rongsmad (Rumei, Markham) and mTsholnga/Thaya (Cuowa, Markham). Sister languages Lamo (Glottolog Lamo) and Drag-yab sMar (Glottolog 'Drag-yab', NOCODE_Dragyab) are distinct languages and are not the basis of the reading.

sources.note: Sec. 2.2 Larong sMar (Phagpa dialect), p. 82: two word tones high and rising; TBU = first two syllables; later syllables atonal (low level); apostrophe marks a second syllable outside the TBU. No mention of stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 record for zlar1234 (classification Chamdoic > Smar; meds: Zhao 2019, Zhao 2018, Changdu Diquzhi 2005; also cites Zhao 2024 CLAO on Dpal.ri Smar and Engels & Bodt 2025 ms. for subgrouping)

Suzuki, Hiroyuki, Tashi Nyima, Sonam Wangmo & Tsering Samdrup. 2024. Suprasegmental features of Lamo and its sister languages: With reference to Kansai Japanese. In Nohara & Ikeda (eds.) Grammatical Phenomena of Sino-Tibetan Languages 6, 67-86. Kyoto University. hdl:2433/289967
sources.note: Treats Lamo, Larong sMar and Drag-yab sMar as tone languages with a two-way H/L register on the word-initial position plus an 'accent nucleus' (falling point between syllables), TBU = first two syllables, likened to Kansai Japanese rather than to stress. On stress it says (p. 79, of Lamo): the neutral-tone / stress-accent analyses of Tibetic 'have not been applied to Lamo; no linguistic realisation supports either the existence or non-existence of stress on a single syllable'. Larong sMar data: Table 3 (numerals 1-20, Rongsmad/Phagpa/Thaya), (25)-(26), Table 4.

sources.citation: Suzuki Hiroyuki, Sonam Wangmo & Tsering Samdrup. 2023. Raron-Ma [Larong sMar] go Cuowa [mTsholnga] hoogen no goi siryoo (Niti-ei taisyoo). Journal of Kijutsuken 15: 33-53. (Japanese)
sources.note: Sec. 2.4, p. 35: same two-way word-tone statement as the 2022 Rongsmad list (high vs low, domain = first two syllables), adding that cases of first-syllable-only tone are few in mTsholnga. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Suzuki Hiroyuki, Sonam Wangmo & Tsering Samdrup. 2022. Raron-Ma [Larong sMar] go Rumei [Rongsmad] hoogen no goi siryoo (Niti-ei taisyoo). Journal of Kijutsuken 14: 27-63. (Japanese)
sources.note: Sec. 2.4 Seichou (tone), p. 30: two word tones, high and low; tone domain = word-initial two syllables, later syllables non-distinctive and mostly low level; (') after syllable 1 when only the first syllable carries distinctive tone; compounds may carry one tone per component. Nothing on stress (kyousei/akusento).

sources.citation: Tashi Nyima & Hiroyuki Suzuki. 2019. Newly recognised languages in Chamdo: Geography, culture, history, and language. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 42(1): 38-81. doi:10.1075/ltba.18004.nyi
sources.note: Geography/history/lexical comparison; Larong sMar appears in sec. 2.2 (distribution) and in lexical tables. Only prosodic remark is fn. 32-33: suprasegmentals follow Kitamura's word-tone system, tones high and rising (for Lamo). No stress statement for any language.

sources.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki & Tashi Nyima. 2018. Historical relationship among three non-Tibetic languages in Chamdo, TAR. Proc. ICSTLL-51, 1-7. Kyoto University. hdl:2433/235308
sources.note: Sec. 2.2 Larong sMar (Tangre Chaya dialect): 'Suprasegmentals: high and rising. A tone bearing unit (TBU) is first two syllables of each word'; apostrophe = second syllable out of TBU. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Zhao, Haoliang. 2018. A brief introduction to Zlarong, a newly recognized language in Mdzo sgang, TAR. Proceedings of the 51st International Conference on Sino-Tibetan Languages and Linguistics, 1053-1060. Kyoto: Kyoto University.
sources.note: 'Phonology overview' gives consonants, vowels and 'Tone: Three-way word tone system: High (55), Falling (53) and Low (31, 13)' with minimal pairs; syllable CV, no clusters. Nothing on stress or accent (the earlier scan called this paper 'not online'; it is open on KURENAI, handle 2433/235318).
